_role: REHBER SOURCE REGISTRY (F-H İŞ 2, 2026-08-23). Every advice the engine prints either carries a number THIS draft measured (basis 'computed:...') or points at a row here (basis 'source:<id>'). guide_completeness_check refuses any advice whose printed numbers are not accounted for by one of the two. coats-seams.title: Coats — Seam Types (ISO 4916 seam classes / ISO 4915 stitch types)
quotes: Class 3 (bound) application: Necklines of t-shirts.
For the seam specification to be meaningful, the designation of the stitch type has to be added after the designation of the stitched seam.
coats-seams.note: The two ISO numbers, the plain-seam pair (1.01.01 + 301), the serging code (6.01.01) and the bound class (3) are all stated verbatim in the source or in knowledge/DIKIS-SOZLUGU-ISO-2026-08-23.md §3. The 2.5 mm stitch length is the standard lockstitch setting quoted alongside; it is a SETTING, not a tolerance, and nothing in the engine reads it.

unl-knits.title: University of Nebraska–Lincoln extension, Sewing With Knits (the 4-inch stretch test)
quotes: stable <12.5%, moderate ~30%, super 50%+ (4-inch test)
plain straight stitch (seams pop; use narrow zigzag 1-1.5mm)
regular needle (use ballpoint 75/11-80/12)
unl-knits.note: Mirrored in knowledge/stitchu.db, table `fabrics`, row 'jersey' (columns stretch / common_mistakes). ⚠ UNL's band edges are NOT the band this engine drafts on — see fabricease.hpp: the F-H card's band is implemented and UNL is recorded as the cross-reference, not averaged in.

iso-4915.title: ISO 4915:1991 — Textiles, Stitch types, classification and terminology
quotes: 6 classes: 100 chain · 200 hand-origin · 300 lockstitch · 400 multi-thread chain · 500 overedge · 600 covering
First digit = class, second and third = type within class.
iso-4915.note: Read in knowledge/DIKIS-SOZLUGU-ISO-2026-08-23.md §2. Only class numbers and 301 are quoted by the engine; a 3-digit type is never invented from the class.

unl-knits+iso-4915.title: UNL Sewing With Knits + ISO 4915:1991 stitch classes (combined advice)
quotes: 6 sınıf: 100 zincir · 200 el kökenli · 300 düz (lock) · 400 çok iplikli zincir · 500 overlok · 600 kaplama

uof-needle-sizes.title: University of Fashion — Sewing Machine Needle Sizes & Diameters (needle size by fabric weight)
quotes: 60 / 8 / 60 / .0245 / Light Weight ... 70 / 10 / 70 / .028 / Light Weight
75 / 11 / 75 / .030 / Medium Weight ... 95 / 15 / 95 / .038 / Medium Weight
100 / 16 / 100 / .040 / Heavy Weight ... 110 / 18 / 110 / .044 / Heavy Weight & Leather
uof-needle-sizes.note: Read verbatim from the PDF with pdftotext -layout on 2026-09-03 (M5-rehber). The chart gives a BAND per weight class, never one number, and the engine prints the band it gives. It does NOT publish the g/m2 edges of 'Light'/'Medium'/'Heavy' — those come from `fabricuk-gsm-bands` and the composition of the two is declared in engine/src/rehber.hpp.

fabricuk-gsm-bands.title: Fabric UK — Understanding Fabric Weight (g/m2 weight classes, ISO 3801 measurement)
quotes: Under 150 GSM is lightweight, 150 to 350 GSM is medium-weight, and over 350 GSM is heavyweight.
Testing follows the ISO 3801 methodology, a recognised international standard.
fabricuk-gsm-bands.note: ⚠ WEAK SOURCE, DECLARED: this is a retailer's guide, not a standard. ISO 3801 defines how g/m2 is MEASURED and publishes no weight CLASSES — the class edges are this page's, and no standards body publishing them was found (searched 2026-09-03: ASTM D3776 and ISO 3801 are both mass-per-area METHODS, same shape as the D3107/D2594 finding in fabric-catalog-v1.json). Used for ONE thing: which row of `uof-needle-sizes` to read. Nothing in the drafted geometry reads it.

schmetz-needle-types.title: SCHMETZ (needle manufacturer) — Sewing Machine Needle Guide, point type by fabric
quotes: Universal: General sewing of knit and woven fabrics.
Jersey/Ball Point: Designed for sewing on knits and some stretch fabrics.
Choose needle size according to thread thickness and needle type according to fabric application.
schmetz-needle-types.note: The manufacturer's own page, read 2026-09-03. Carries the POINT TYPE (universal vs ballpoint) only; SCHMETZ explicitly ties size to thread thickness and type to application, and publishes no fabric-weight-to-size table — which is why the size comes from `uof-needle-sizes` / `unl-knits` and not from here.

uof-needle-sizes+fabricuk-gsm-bands+schm.title: Needle for a WOVEN — three documents composed (M5-rehber, 2026-09-03)
quotes: weight class <- g/m2 (fabricuk-gsm-bands) -> size band (uof-needle-sizes) -> point type (schmetz-needle-types)
uof-needle-sizes+fabricuk-gsm-bands+schm.note: No ONE publication answers 'which needle for this bolt'. Three do, in a chain, and the chain is written here rather than hidden in the sentence: the weight in g/m2 picks a class, the class picks a SIZE BAND, the knit/woven word picks the POINT. The engine never narrows the band further — see engine/src/rehber.hpp section 3.

unl-knits+fabricuk-gsm-bands+schmetz-nee.title: Needle for a KNIT — UNL sizes, gsm class, SCHMETZ point (M5-rehber, 2026-09-03)
quotes: For lightweight knits use 75/11, medium weight use 80/12 and heavy weight, 90/14.
unl-knits+fabricuk-gsm-bands+schmetz-nee.note: A knit-specific table beats a general one, so the SIZE here is UNL's single number per class, not the University of Fashion band. The class edge in g/m2 is still fabricuk-gsm-bands (weak, declared there) and the point type is SCHMETZ.
